A. To hold "the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels".

B. To pursue efforts "to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels".
x: Both are Paris goals: well below 2°C (A) and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C (B).

s: In the COP 21 convention held at Paris, it was proposed to limit the level of global warming to
o: 3 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
1 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
2 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
4 degree centigrade above pre industrial levels
x: COP21 Paris set the limit at 2°C above pre-industrial levels (well below 2°C, aiming for 1.5°C).

src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
s: The operating entity of the financial mechanism of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) which is intended to be the main fund for global climate change finance in the context of mobilizing USD 100 billion by 2020 is:
x: The Green Climate Fund is the operating entity of the UNFCCC financial mechanism and was the centrepiece of the US$100 billion-a-year-by-2020 goal. The Standing Committee on Finance and the Special Climate Change Fund are not that main fund.

s: BioCarbon Fund Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscapes is managed by the:
x: The BioCarbon Fund Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscapes is a multilateral fund backed by donor governments and managed by the World Bank.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding ‘Green Climate Fund’ is/are correct?

I. It is intended to assist the developing countries in adaptation and mitigation practices to counter climate change.

II. It is founded under the aegis of UNEP, OECD, Asian Development Bank and World Bank.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: I is correct: the GCF helps developing countries with adaptation and mitigation. II is wrong: the GCF was founded under the UNFCCC COP (Cancún 2010), not under UNEP, OECD, ADB and the World Bank.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect for ‘Green Climate Fund” (GCF)?
o: It was established in the Durban Conference on
It would support programs and policies in developing
The developed nations would provide the fund
The fund will start operating from, 2014
x: The GCF was set up at COP16 in Cancún (2010), not Durban; Durban (COP17, 2011) only approved its governing instrument. So statement 1 is the incorrect one.

s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) estimates that global warming is likely to reach ____ between 2030 and 2052.
x: The IPCC SR1.5 (2018) found that at current rates warming is likely to reach 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052.

s: According to the IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) report on global warming, global net human-caused emissions of carbon dioxide would need to reach ____ by 2050 from 2010 levels.
x: SR1.5 says that for 1.5°C global net CO₂ emissions must fall about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030 and reach net zero by about 2050.

s: In 2012, which country of the followings was with the lowest GHG Emitters on per capita basis is
x: India's per-capita GHG emissions are far below those of the USA, UK and China (about 2.9 t CO₂e versus 18 t for the USA and 11 t for China), so India was the lowest of the four.

s: Which of the following is not true for India to combat the adverse impact of Climate Change?
o: Establishment of the Clean Development Mechanism
Investment of Rs. 100 crores as an initial corpus under
Not attended the 19th Meeting of BASIC at Sun City,
x: India attended the 19th BASIC ministerial meeting at Sun City, South Africa, so 'not attended' is the untrue statement. The other options are steps India did take.

s: Published annually since 2005, the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) tracks countries' efforts to combat climate change. What was India's rank on the index in 2019?
x:
Most keys: 9th (the index released in 2019, i.e. CCPI 2020). Strictly the edition named 'CCPI 2019' (released Dec 2018 at COP24) placed India 11th (app notes 5:96 sub 6; gktoday.in).
The CCPI released in 2019 (CCPI 2020, at COP25 Madrid on 10 Dec 2019) ranked India 9th, the first time India entered the top 10. The 2019 edition, released in Dec 2018, had India 11th, which is not among the options.

s: What is India's rank in "Climate change Performance Index" (CCPI) 2017?
x: In the CCPI 2017, released in November 2016 by Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and CAN, India was ranked 20th among 58 countries.

s: According to the 2017 Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) published by Germanwatch, India's rank among 58 countries in the world is?
x: India was ranked 20th among 58 countries in the CCPI 2017 released by Germanwatch in November 2016. It rose to 14th in 2018 and 11th in 2019.

s: The place of India among 58 Countries of the world as per 2017 Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) published by the German watch is:
x: In the 2017 CCPI (Germanwatch), India was placed 20th among 58 countries. 21st-23rd are distractors.

s: Choose the correct statement with respect to C40 CITIES.
o: It is a global mission to limit the global heating to 0.5° Celsius.
It has partner of 106 cities of the world representing half of the global economy.
It is a network of the world's megacities committed to addressing climate change.
The deadline to achieve its goals is 2026.
x: C40 Cities is a network of the world's megacities committed to addressing climate change. It is not a 0.5°C mission and has no 2026 deadline.

s: As per Climate Change Performance Index, 2017, Which of the following is among the best performers in industrialized nations?
x: In the CCPI 2017 the UK was among the better-performing industrialised nations, while Australia, Canada and Japan were ranked among the poor performers.

s: Which of the following countries recently became the 119th country to join the International Solar Alliance (ISA)?
x: Malta became the 119th member of the International Solar Alliance in February 2024 (membership 125 by March 2026).

s: In which of the following cities was the first summit of 'International Solar Alliance' held ?
x: The ISA was launched at COP21 in Paris (2015), but its first summit (Founding Conference) was held in New Delhi on 11 March 2018. So New Delhi, not Paris.

s: At which of the following places is the Secretariat of the International Solar Alliance (I.S.A.) located at present?
x: The ISA Secretariat is at Gurugram, Haryana. It is the first treaty-based intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India; it was launched in Paris but is not based there.

s: The first summit of 'International Solar Alliance' was held in which of the following cities?
x: The first International Solar Alliance Summit was held in New Delhi on 11 March 2018. Paris was where the ISA was launched at COP21 in 2015.

src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
s: Where is the head quarters of International Solar Alliance, an Intergovernmental Organization to promote solar energy is located?
x: The International Solar Alliance, launched by India and France at COP21 (2015), is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana. It is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.

s:
What is true about 'Panchamitra promises' taken by government of India for climate change?

I. Increasing Non-fossil energy Capacity to 250 gigawatts by 2030.

II. Providing 50 per cent of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030.

III. Reduction of total projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes from now to 2030.

IV. Reduction of the carbon intensity of the economy by 45 per cent by 2030.

V. Achieving the target of net zero emissions by 2045.
o: Only I and V are correct
Only II, III and IV are correct
Only I, II, III and IV are correct
Only II, III, IV and V are correct
x: Panchamrit: 500 GW non-fossil capacity (not 250 GW), 50% of energy from renewables, 1 billion tonnes cut in projected emissions and a 45% cut in carbon intensity by 2030, and net zero by 2070 (not 2045). So only II, III and IV are true.

s: It means that a country will bring down its emissions to zero by 2050. 2. It means that a country's emissions will be compensated by the absorption and removal of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes :
x: Net zero means residual emissions are balanced by absorption and removal of greenhouse gases, so statement 2 is correct. It does not mean emissions fall to zero by 2050 for every country (India's year is 2070), so statement 1 is wrong.

s: What is not true about the commitment made by India at UNFCC COP 26 Conference?
o: By 2030, India will reduce its carbon emission by one
By 2030, India will meet 60% of its total energy
By 2030, India will increase its non-fossil energy
x: At COP26 India pledged to meet 50% of its energy requirements from renewables by 2030, not 60%, so that option is not true. The 1 billion tonne cut and the 500 GW non-fossil capacity are real Panchamrit pledges.

src: APPSC 2022 Various posts under Group-IV Services(Limited Rec
s: As per the updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) as of August, 2022 India to reduce Emissions Intensity of its GDP by ______ by 2030.
x: India's updated NDC of August 2022 raised the emissions-intensity cut of GDP to 45% by 2030 from the 2005 level (INDC 2015: 33-35%). 50% is the non-fossil capacity share, not the intensity cut.

s: ‘Intended Nationally Determined Contribution’ sometimes seen in news refers to
o: Promise made by European countries for rehabilitation of refugees from middle East.
World action plan to deal with Climate change.
Equity share holding of member countries in AIIB.
World action plan for sustainable development goals.
x: An INDC is each country's own pledged post-2020 climate action plan, submitted before COP21 Paris, so it is the world climate-change action plan. Refugees, AIIB shares and SDGs are unrelated.

src: AP Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I 2017
s: Which of the following is an effective positive measure of climate change?
o: Expansion of carbon sink through afforestation
x: Afforestation expands carbon sinks that absorb CO2, a direct positive climate measure (India's NDC carbon-sink goal). Subsidising electricity raises emissions; removing all fuel subsidies or banning narcotics is not a climate measure.

s: What is true about Mission LiFE program of government of India?
o: It is India-led global mass movement to nudge individual and community action to protect and preserve the environment.
It was first launched in the state of Maharashtra.
The program was launched by the president of India.
x: Mission LiFE is an India-led global mass movement to nudge individual and community action for the environment. It was launched on 20 October 2022 at Kevadia, Gujarat, by the Prime Minister with the UN Secretary-General, so the other options are wrong.

s: 'Eco Club' programme is one of the major components of which of the following Central sector schemes, launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: Environment Education, Awareness and Training scheme
x: Eco-Clubs under the National Green Corps are a component of MoEFCC's central sector scheme 'Environment Education, Awareness and Training' (EEAT, launched 1983-84).

s: According to Jharkhand Action Plan on Climate Change Report (2014) which is the most sensitive district?
x: The Jharkhand Action Plan on Climate Change (2014) identified Seraikela-Kharsawan as the most climate-sensitive district.

s: When did Fridays for Future Andhra Pradesh (FFFAP) participate in the first Global strike
x: Fridays For Future Andhra Pradesh joined the first global climate strike in 2019.

s: What is the full form of FFFAP, working for creating climate change awareness in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Full days For Future Andhra Pradesh
Fine days For Future Andhra Pradesh
Fast days For Future Andhra Pradesh
x: FFFAP stands for Fridays For Future Andhra Pradesh, the youth group creating climate-change awareness in AP that joined the first global climate strike in 2019.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Government created an exclusive Climate Change Cell (CCC) in _______.
x: Andhra Pradesh created an exclusive Climate Change Cell in November 2022; it now works as the AP State Climate Change Cell under the Department of Environment, Forests and Science & Technology.

s: In which year did Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh release India's first National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), outlining existing and future policies and programmes addressing climate mitigation and adaptation?
x: PM Dr Manmohan Singh released India's first National Action Plan on Climate Change on 30 June 2008. 2010 is the launch of the National Solar Mission.

s: How many national missions have been started as 68. Aft part of the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
x: The NAPCC (2008) has eight National Missions as its core. The Economic Survey 2025-26 mentions a ninth (climate change and human health), but the standard answer is 8.

s: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) aims to address
o: Mitigation and adaptation strategies for climate change
x: The NAPCC combines mitigation (solar, energy efficiency, habitat) and adaptation (water, agriculture, Himalaya, Green India), not just emissions, biodiversity or air pollution.

s: What is the important change for the present generation of politics of the entire World?
x: Climate change is widely called the defining political issue of the present generation for the entire world. 'Environmental crisis' is broader and vaguer; separation of states and social justice are not global changes.

src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
s: India’s National Action Plan on climate change did NOT include:
o: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency
National Mission for Sustaining the Coastal and Marine Ecosystem
x: The National Mission for Sustaining the Coastal and Marine Ecosystem is not one of the eight NAPCC missions; coastal areas were only proposed later. Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Sustainable Habitat are core missions.

s: Which one of the following is not included in Eight Missions under India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change?
x: Nuclear power is not one of the eight NAPCC missions. Solar is the National Solar Mission, afforestation is the Green India Mission, and power from urban waste falls under the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat.

s: Which of the following is not listed under eight action of Climate Action Plan of Government of India?
x: Atomic (nuclear) energy is not among the eight NAPCC missions. Solar energy (National Solar Mission), afforestation (Green India) and waste-to-energy (part of the Sustainable Habitat mission) are covered.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: When was the National Solar Mission Launched?
x: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010, not with the NAPCC in 2008.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: National Mission for a Green India is merged with:
x: The Green India Mission is implemented in convergence with MGNREGA (and CAMPA funds) for afforestation work; this is the printed answer, though 'converged' is more accurate than 'merged'.

s: National Mission for Green India has been initiated in the following states by Governments of India with the aim to improve the density of existing forests.
x: The Green India Mission is implemented through State perspective plans, and both Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh had plans approved to improve the density of existing forests.

s:
If National Water Mission is properly and completely implemented, how will it impact the country?

I. Part of the water needs of urban areas will be met through recycling of waste water.

II. The water requirements of coastal cities with inadequate alternative sources of water will be met by adopting appropriate technologies that allow for the use of Ocean water.

III. All the rivers of Himalayan origin will be linked to the rivers of peninsular India.

IV. The expenses incurred by farmers for digging bore-wells and for installing motors and pump sets to draw ground water will be completely reimbursed by the Government.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: The National Water Mission aims to meet part of urban water needs by recycling waste water and to meet coastal cities' needs through new technologies such as low-temperature desalination, so I and II. River interlinking and full reimbursement of farmers' bore-well costs are not NWM goals (UPSC key: b).

s:
Which of the following best describe/describes the aim of ‘Green India Mission’ of the Government of India?

I. Incorporating environmental benefits and costs into the Union and State Budgets thereby implementing the ‘green accounting’.

II. Launching the second green revolution to enhance agricultural output so as to ensure food security to one and all in the future.

III. Restoring and enhancing forest cover and responding to climate change by a combination of adaptation and mitigation measurers.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Green India Mission aims to protect, restore and enhance forest cover and respond to climate change through adaptation and mitigation, so only III. Green accounting and a second green revolution are not its aims (UPSC key: c).

s: 'India climate change knowledge portal' was launched in which of the following months of 2020?
x: MoEFCC launched the India Climate Change Knowledge Portal in November 2020 to show all major government climate-related actions in one place.

s: In which of the following year, United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) was founded?
x: UNEP was created in 1972 after the UN Conference on the Human Environment at Stockholm (5-16 June 1972).

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: In which year was the Survey of India established?
x: The Survey of India, the national mapping agency, was set up in 1767.

src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men

o: Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE)
The Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)
Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N)
Advanced Centre for Integrated Water Resources Management (ACIWRM)
x: The State of India's Environment report is published annually by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE), New Delhi, together with Down To Earth.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: In which city, the Zoological Survey of India is located?
x: The Zoological Survey of India (1916) is headquartered in Kolkata, as is the Botanical Survey of India.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: How many new species were discovered from India in the year 2018 as per data released by Botanical Survey of India (BSI) and the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)?
x: BSI and ZSI reported 596 new species from India in 2018: 372 animals (Animal Discoveries 2018) and 224 plants (Plant Discoveries 2018).

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

s: Forest Research Institute is located in :

s: Minimata disease is caused due to the heavy metal
x: Minamata disease is mercury poisoning from methyl mercury in fish, first found in Minamata, Japan, in 1956. Lead, cadmium (itai-itai) and arsenic (black-foot) cause other diseases.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which gas causes industrial disasters?
x: Industrial disasters such as Bhopal (MIC) and LG Polymers (styrene) are mostly toxic gas leaks. Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are not the usual cause.

s: What was the most recent worst man-made industrial disaster in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The LG Polymers styrene vapour leak at R.R. Venkatapuram, Visakhapatnam, on 7 May 2020 is the most recent worst man-made industrial disaster in AP. The Mayapuri radiological accident (2010) was in Delhi.

s: Which of the following gas was responsible for the Bhopal Gas tragedy?

s: Which poisonous gas killed thousands of people in Bhopal gas tragedy?
x: The Bhopal gas tragedy of 2-3 December 1984 was caused by leakage of methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas from the Union Carbide pesticide plant. Not cyanogen chloride, hydrogen cyanide, H2S, NO2, SO2 or CO.

x: The Bhopal gas tragedy of 2-3 December 1984 was caused by leakage of methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas from the Union Carbide pesticide plant. Not cyanogen chloride, hydrogen cyanide, H2S, NO2, SO2 or CO.

s: When did the Bhopal Gas tragedy happen?

src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
s: By recycling paper, plastic and metals, we can reduce the following pollution?
x: Recycling paper, plastic and metal keeps solid waste out of landfills and dumps, so it mainly reduces soil (land) pollution. It also eases air and water pollution, so 'cannot reduce' is wrong.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following is a primary source of air pollution in cities?
x: Vehicle exhaust (CO, NOx, hydrocarbons, PM) is a primary source of urban air pollution. Wind, ocean waves and tree respiration are not pollution sources.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s:
Which of the following is/are the likely impact of nitrogen pollution?

a. Loss of biodiversity

b. Pollution of rivers and seas

c. Ozone depletion
x: Reactive nitrogen from fertilisers and combustion causes biodiversity loss, eutrophication of rivers and seas, and ozone depletion (N2O). So all three.

s:
Match the pollution type with its major source.
Pollution Type:

a. Air Pollution

b. Water Pollution

c. Soil Pollution

d. Noise Pollution
Major Source:

I. Sewage

II. Industrial emissions

III. Use of chemical fertilizers

IV. Construction activities
x: Air pollution – industrial emissions; water pollution – sewage; soil pollution – chemical fertilisers; noise pollution – construction. So a-II, b-I, c-III, d-IV.

s: Which one of the following is not an anthropogenic cause of air pollution?
o: Sewers and domestic drains emanating foul gases
Pollen grains from flowers in air
Power stations using coal or crude oil
x: Pollen grains are a natural source of air pollution. Pesticide residues, foul gases from sewers and coal or oil power stations are man-made (anthropogenic).

s: Which of the following is a potential harmful effect of agro-chemicals on the environment?
x: Fertiliser and pesticide runoff and leaching pollute surface and groundwater (eutrophication, nitrates), a harmful effect. Higher fertility, better growth and less erosion are not harmful effects.

src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
s:
Given below are two statements. Identify the CORRECT statement (s).
I. Sewage treatment plants are one of the examples of a sustainable technology designed to address water pollution.
II. Air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions are the primary environmental concerns associated with the widespread use of fossil fuels for energy production.
x: Sewage treatment plants are a sustainable technology against water pollution, since sewage is a main water pollutant. Burning fossil fuels causes air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. Both statements are correct.

s: The highest chemical pollution is caused by the industrial effluents of :
x: The leather (tanning) industry's effluents, rich in chromium and other chemicals, cause the highest chemical pollution of water and soil among the options.

s: Indiscriminate use of fertilisers have led to
x: Indiscriminate fertiliser use degrades soil, its runoff pollutes water, and ammonia/N2O pollute the air. So all of these.

s: Effect of pollution is marked on
x: Pollution disturbs the natural balance, natural geochemical cycles and the natural flora of a place, so all of the above.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: Extraction of mineral resources causes
x: Mining clears land (biodiversity loss), exposes soil to erosion and releases acid and heavy-metal drainage (water pollution). So all of the above.

s: Indiscriminate use of fertilizers has led to :
x: Chemical fertilisers degrade soil, leach into surface and ground water, and release ammonia and nitrous oxide into air. So all of the above.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s:
Match
List-I (Environmental Pollutants) with
List-II (Prevention & control measures/Acts/rules).
List-I:

(a) Emission of poisonous gases

(b) Green tax

(c) Untreated water

(d) Plastic waste
List-II:
(i) Coagulation
(ii) Catalytic converters
(iii) Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021
(iv) Old vehicles
x: Catalytic converters cut poisonous exhaust gases, a green tax targets old vehicles, coagulation treats untreated water and the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021 deal with plastic waste. So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

s: Which of the following is a biodegradable pollutant?
x: Sewage is organic and is decomposed by microbes, so it is biodegradable. Asbestos, DDT and plastic are non-biodegradable.

s: Which of the following is a biodegradable pollutant?
x: Sewage is a biodegradable pollutant broken down by micro-organisms. Asbestos, plastic and polythene are non-biodegradable.

s: Which one among the following industries produces the most non- biodegradable wastes?
x: Thermal power plants generate huge amounts of fly ash, a non-biodegradable waste, more than food processing, textile or paper units.

s: Which one of the following is not biodegradable?
x: Silver foil is a metal that microbes cannot break down, so it is not biodegradable. Wool, leather and jute are natural organic materials that decompose.

s: Dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane (DDT) is a :
x: DDT is a persistent organochlorine insecticide that does not break down naturally and biomagnifies, so it is a non-biodegradable pollutant.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Which of the following is biodegradable pollutant?
x: Natural rubber is a plant polymer that microbes decompose, so it is biodegradable. Plastic, polythene and mercury are non-biodegradable.

s: Which one of the following pollutes the air of a big city?
x: Lead from vehicle exhaust (leaded petrol) pollutes the air of big cities. Copper, chromium and calcium are not typical urban air pollutants.

s: Workers of paint industry are exposed to which one of the following hazards?
x: Paints contain lead pigments, so paint-industry workers face lead exposure; MoEFCC caps lead in household paints at 90 ppm.

s: Gold mining activity is a source of mercury pollution in the world. 2. Coal-based thermal power plants cause mercury pollution. 3. There is no known safe level of exposure to mercury. How many of the above statements are correct ?
x:
Most keys (printed key, Vajiram, GKToday): Only two. PMF IAS and Dalvoy: All three, reading 'no known safe level of exposure' as correct (PMF Environment Part 05 p.14).
Gold mining (amalgamation) and coal-based power plants are major mercury sources, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is treated as not correct by most keys because permissible exposure limits for mercury exist, giving 'only two'.

s:
Mercury is a toxic substance that severely contaminates land, water, air and the food chain. Which among the following is/are source(s) of mercury pollution?
I. Pesticides
II. Dental amalgam fillings
III. Fluorescent lamp
IV. Coal-based thermal power plants
o: I, II, III and IV all
x: Pesticides, dental amalgam fillings, fluorescent lamps and coal-based thermal power plants are all sources of mercury pollution.

s: Corrosion of marble of Taj Mahal due to acid rain caused by pollutants is called as?
x: Acid rain from SO2 and NOx reacts with the calcium carbonate of the Taj Mahal's marble, causing pitting and yellowing called marble cancer.

s:
Match
List-I (Pollution) with
List-II (Pollutant):

a. Marble Cancer

b. Biomagnification

c. Green house effect

d. Lung cancer

I. Methane

II. Nickel

III. Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide

IV. Chlorohydrocarbons
x: Marble cancer – SO2 and NO2 (acid rain); biomagnification – chlorinated hydrocarbons; greenhouse effect – methane; lung cancer – nickel. So III IV I II.
